chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who bought an orchard containing palm trees and other trees, some of which had already borne fruit and some of which had not borne fruit. He said: “There is no harm in it if there are some in it that have already borne fruit.”

key_terms.بُسْتَانًا: an orchard or garden being sold
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no legal objection or harm in it
key_terms.نَخْلٌ: date palm trees in the orchard

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy an orchard when only some of its trees have already borne fruit?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the purchase of an orchard containing a mix of trees, some fruit-bearing and some not yet fruit-bearing. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that such a sale is permissible when the orchard includes trees that have already borne fruit.
